title: Sequences
description: Animated KS3 Maths lesson on sequences for ages 9 to 14: terms and term-to-term rules, multiplying rules, square and triangle numbers, Fibonacci, growing patterns and finding and using the nth term.
intro: Spot the pattern and keep it going! Term-to-term rules, special sequences, growing patterns and the nth term, explained by the owl in five short parts.

steps.say: A **sequence** is a list of numbers that follows a rule. Each number in it is called a **term**.
Look at the jumps: 4, 9, 14, 19 goes up by 5 each time. The **term-to-term rule** is "add 5".

steps.speak: So the next term is 19 plus 5, which is 24.

steps.say: Sequences can go down too. 50, 44, 38, 32 goes down by 6 each time, so the next term is 32 − 6 = **26**.
steps.speak: Sequences can go down too. 50, 44, 38, 32 goes down by 6 each time, so the next term is 32 minus 6, which is 26.

check.hint: How much does it go up by each time?
check.explain: It goes up by 4 each time: 19 + 4 = **23**.

steps.say: Some rules multiply. In 3, 6, 12, 24 each term is **double** the one before. The rule is "multiply by 2".
The gaps are 3, 6 and 12. They are not all the same, so the rule is not "add a number".
2, 6, 18, 54 has the rule "multiply by 3". The next terms are 54 × 3 = 162, then 162 × 3 = **486**.
steps.speak: 2, 6, 18, 54 has the rule multiply by 3. The next terms are 54 times 3, which is 162, then 162 times 3, which is 486.

check.q: What is the term-to-term rule for 5, 10, 20, 40, …?
check.hint: The gaps are 5, 10, 20. Are they the same? Compare each term with the one before.
check.explain: Each term is double the one before: 5 × 2 = 10, 10 × 2 = 20, 20 × 2 = 40. The rule is **multiply by 2**.

steps.say: **Square numbers**: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25. They make squares of dots: 1 × 1, 2 × 2, 3 × 3, and so on.
steps.speak: Square numbers: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25. They make squares of dots: 1 times 1, 2 times 2, 3 times 3, and so on.

steps.say: **Triangle numbers**: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15. Each new row has one more dot, so the gaps grow: 2, 3, 4, 5.
The **Fibonacci** sequence: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8. Each term is the two before it added together, so the next one is 5 + 8 = **13**.
steps.speak: The Fibonacci sequence: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8. Each term is the two before it added together, so the next one is 5 plus 8, which is 13.

check.hint: The 3rd square number is 3 × 3. What is the 7th?
check.explain: The 7th square number is 7 × 7 = **49**. (36 is the 6th and 64 is the 8th.)

steps.say: Here is a growing pattern. Pattern 1 has 3 squares, Pattern 2 has 5 and Pattern 3 has 7.
Each new pattern adds **2** squares: one on each arm.
For Pattern 10, start with 3 and add 2 nine more times: 3 + 9 × 2 = 3 + 18 = **21**.
steps.speak: For Pattern 10, start with 3 and add 2 nine more times: 3 plus 9 times 2, which is 3 plus 18, which is 21.

steps.say: The rule for Pattern n is **2n + 1**: n squares on each arm, plus the corner. Pattern 10: 2 × 10 + 1 = 21.
steps.speak: The rule for Pattern n is 2 n plus 1: n squares on each arm, plus the corner. Pattern 10: 2 times 10, plus 1, equals 21.

check.q: Patterns 1, 2 and 3 have 5, 8 and 11 squares. How many squares will Pattern 4 have?
check.hint: How many squares are added each time?

steps.say: The **nth term** is a rule that gives any term from its position, n. For 3n + 1, the 1st term is 3 × 1 + 1 = 4. Then come 7 and 10.
steps.speak: The nth term is a rule that gives any term from its position, n. For 3 n plus 1, the 1st term is 3 times 1, plus 1, which is 4. Then come 7 and 10.

steps.say: The 10th term is 3 × 10 + 1 = **31**. No need to write out all ten terms!
steps.speak: The 10th term is 3 times 10, plus 1, which is 31. No need to write out all ten terms!

steps.say: Finding the rule: 5, 8, 11, 14 goes up by 3, so compare it with **3n**: 3, 6, 9, 12. Every term is 2 more, so the nth term is **3n + 2**.
steps.speak: Finding the rule: 5, 8, 11, 14 goes up by 3, so compare it with 3 n: 3, 6, 9, 12. Every term is 2 more, so the nth term is 3 n plus 2.

steps.say: 10, 8, 6, 4 goes down by 2, so compare it with **−2n**: −2, −4, −6, −8. Every term is 12 more, so the nth term is **12 − 2n**.
steps.speak: 10, 8, 6, 4 goes down by 2, so compare it with negative 2 n: negative 2, negative 4, negative 6, negative 8. Every term is 12 more, so the nth term is 12 minus 2 n.

steps.say: Is 50 a term of 4n + 1? Try 4n + 1 = 50. Then 4n = 49 and n = 12.25. That is not a whole number, so **no**, 50 is not a term.
steps.speak: Is 50 a term of 4 n plus 1? Try 4 n plus 1 equals 50. Then 4 n equals 49, and n equals 12 point 2 5. That is not a whole number, so no, 50 is not a term.

check.q: What is the nth term of 4, 9, 14, 19, …?
check.hint: It goes up by 5, so compare it with 5n: 5, 10, 15, 20. How far off is each term?
check.explain: 5n gives 5, 10, 15, 20. Each term is 1 less, so the nth term is **5n − 1**. Check: 5 × 1 − 1 = 4.
